questions.q: Which incident would you most hate to find out about from someone outside?
questions.why: Anchors the log sources that matter.
questions.need: The incident nobody wants to hear about from outside is covered
questions.how: Map the sources and detections that would catch it

questions.q: How long did the last real investigation take, from alert to answer?
questions.why: Investigation time is what the platform must cut.
questions.how: Time one investigation and remove the slowest step

questions.q: Which environments send no logs at all today?
questions.why: Blind spots are the first gap to close.

questions.q: Do you know which log sources are expected for each environment, and which are missing?
questions.why: A list of expected sources makes silence visible.
questions.need: Expected log sources are listed, and missing ones are visible
questions.how: Write the expected list per environment

questions.q: How many detections are switched on, and how many have fired in the last month?
questions.why: Rules that never fire may be broken, not quiet.
questions.need: Detections that are on actually fire when they should
questions.how: Test the top detections with safe simulations

questions.q: Are response playbooks automated for the most common alerts?
questions.why: Automation decides how much the team can handle.
questions.need: Common alerts are handled by automated playbooks
questions.how: Automate the three most frequent responses

questions.q: How long are logs kept, and is that enough for an investigation or an auditor?
questions.why: Retention gaps appear at the worst moment.
questions.need: Logs are kept long enough for an investigation and an audit
questions.how: Agree retention with legal and the auditors

questions.q: How many alerts are closed without anyone looking, and who decides that?
questions.need: No alert is closed without someone deciding
questions.how: Make closure need a reason and an owner
